data.narrative:
Natilus is a Series A autonomous aircraft company operating in the Drones & Autonomous sector. The company has raised $16M to date. The broader sector includes 8 private peers—notably Waymo, Wayve, Zipline, Joby Aviation, and Nuro—and no public comparables, limiting the available valuation reference set.

Given data constraints, a single methodologically sound approach applies. The Stage-Progression method uses the $16M total capital raised as a baseline proxy and applies a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical of Series A-to-next-round valuation progression, yielding $32M. A Peer-Median approach was not applicable; while 7 same-sector peers exist, none yielded three or more datapoints meeting same-stage, adjacent-stage, or similar-tier filters. Relying on all-sector median would introduce unacceptable breadth bias given stage and business model dispersion across autonomous vehicle, delivery, and aviation subsegments.

The triangulation analysis, constrained to one method, supports a median valuation of $32M, with a sensitivity range of $27M to $37M reflecting typical variance around stage-progression assumptions. Key uncertainties remain: the absence of narrowly comparable late-stage funding rounds limits confidence in the 2.0x multiplier's applicability to this specific aircraft segment, and capital intensity and commercialization timelines in autonomous aviation differ materially from consumer drone and ground robotics comparables. A fuller valuation would benefit from additional Series A or late-stage funding data within cargo and passenger autonomous aircraft.
